# enum-not-enforced

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: on

## Why

The model promises a field holds only a fixed set of values, and code switches over them without a fallback. Unless the database refuses other values, any writer can store a string the application has never heard of and break that code later. The database enforces the set through a native enum type (PostgreSQL enum, MySQL ENUM) or a CHECK constraint listing the values.

## Fix

Keep the enum in the model and regenerate the migration so the column becomes a native enum or gets a CHECK (col IN (...)) listing exactly the model's values. Fix existing rows with other values first.

## Exception

A column that intentionally accepts more values than the model while a new value is rolled out, or whose values are policed by a lookup table; write the reason down. A database set that differs from the model's, not only a missing one, is reported too: the finding lists what the database allows.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain enum-not-enforced`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
